title: Knowledge of emergency nurses and related factors toward geriatric: a cross-sectional study
creator: Azam Al-Sadat Asri, Mohammad Reza Yeganeh Rastekanary, Saman Maroufizadeh, Pooyan Ghorbani Vajargah, Samad Karkhah, Nazila Javadi-Pashaki
description: Background:This study aimed to evaluate the geriatric knowledge of emergency nurses and related factors.Materials and methods:This cross-sectional study was conducted on nursing students at Guilan University of Medical Sciences in Iran. The objective was to assess the geriatric knowledge of nurses working in the emergency departments of educational and therapeutic centers in Rasht City.

title: Shared latent representations of speech production for cross-patient speech decoding
creator: Z. Spalding, S. Duraivel, S. Rahimpour, C. Wang, K. Barth, C. Schmitz, S. P. Lad, A. H. Friedman, D. G. Southwell, J. Viventi, G. B. Cogan
description: Speech brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) can restore communication in individuals with neuromotor disorders who are unable to speak. However, current speech BCIs limit patient usability and successful deployment by requiring large volumes of patient-specific data collected over long periods of time. A promising solution to facilitate usability and accelerate their successful deployment is to combine data from multiple patients.

title: Sports Injuries and Care Provided by the Physiotherapy Service of the Brazilian Olympic Committee (BOC) during the Rio de Janeiro 2016 Olympic Summer Games
creator: Flavia Rocco Siqueira, Ronaldo Alves da Cunha, Ana Carolina Ramos e Côrte, Henrique Jorge Jatobá Barreto, Carlos Vicente Andreoli
description: BackgroundUnderstanding previous experiences of athletes regarding treatments is important for preparation for major sporting events. However, there is little evidence regarding the description of physiotherapy services provided at Olympic Games. Providing data may assist with better understanding of the physiotherapy services provided during major sporting events such as the Summer Olympics.

title: Avis de décès pour octobre 2025
creator: Unknown
description: y of Toronto, 1953; médecine familiale. Décédé le 28 août 2025 à l’âge de 96 ans. https://www.fawcettfuneralhomes.com/memorials/stanley-bain/5633832/index.php Botha, Daniel J., Calgary (Alb.); diplôme de médecine, 1983; médecine familiale. Décédé le 12 juin 2025 à l’âge de 65 ans. https://www.mhfh.com/obituaries/Daniel-Johannes-Botha?obId=42939435 Brook, J. Roger, St. Catharines (Ont.); Marine marchande britannique, Seconde Guerre mondiale; University of London (Angleterre), 1953; médecine générale.

title: Triple IFN pathway deficiency sensitizes mice to human respiratory virus infection independent of human viral receptor expression
creator: Qinghong Fan, Meifang Pan, Mengling Jiang, Chengqian Feng, Jianping Cui, Jun Zhang, Shiquan Liang, Yaping Wang, Jingrong Shi, Rui Li, Wei Zhang, Liqiang Feng, Haisheng Yu, Yi-Ping Li, Fengyu Hu, Xiaoping Tang, Hongbo Guo, Feng Li
description: Interferon (IFN) pathways form the innate barrier against viral invasion and partial deficiency in these pathways allows human virus infection. Whether a complete IFN pathway deficiency could confer the susceptibility to human viral infection independent of expressing the human viral receptor remains unknown.

title: Total Laparoscopic Excision of a Large Tailgut Cyst
creator: Ajay Nimbalkar, Anand Zingade, Balaji Dhaigude
description: Tailgut cysts are rare congenital cysts that develop from the embryological remnants of the gut. They are usually found in the retrorectal space. In most of the cases, they are asymptomatic. The treatment of choice for tailgut cysts is complete surgical excision and both open and laparoscopic approaches have been described in the literature.

title: High-gain and broadband in vivo amplifiers enabled by matched materials
creator: Yuting Zheng, Qi Li, Xinyue Wang, Chengwen Wu, Ju-Peng Chen, Zhibo Ren, Yiheng Chen, Xiran Pan, Xun Lei, Wenlong Li, Zhiyuan Xiong, Gao-Yang Ge, Wenxi Sun, Peiyun Li, Suqing Gao, Biqin Yang, Siqi Fang, Jingcao Xu, Jia-Tong Li, Xiaochuan Dai, Ting Lei, Zhi Zhang
description: In-sensor biosignal amplification could enable superior signal quality, lower data transmission redundancy, and enhanced device integration. Organic electrochemical transistor (OECT)-based circuits offer an attractive candidate due to their low-voltage operation, high transduction efficiency, and seamless interfacing with biological tissues. However, the fundamental design principles governing high-performance OECT-based amplifiers, particularly the coupling between material design and circuit-level performance, remain insufficiently understood.

title: Fish oil-derived fatty acids in pregnancy and brain metabolism in middle childhood: results from a randomized controlled trial
creator: M. Hernández-Lorca, MB. Vestergaard, KS. Ambrosen, JM. Raghava, U. Lindberg, JR. Møllegaard Jepsen, JB. Rosenberg, CK. Lemvigh, P. Mohammadzadeh, BY. Glenthøj, B. Chawes, RK. Vinding, K. Bønnelykke, HBW. Larsson, BH. Ebdrup
description: Maternal blood levels of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA) during pregnancy have been associated with brain health outcomes in offspring, but causal effects of PUFA on brain metabolism is unexplored. We examined the effect of maternal PUFA supplementation on brain metabolism in children at age 10, measured as cerebral blood flow (CBF), oxygen consumption (CMRO₂), and brain lactate concentration.

title: Government partnerships with corporate virtual primary care
creator: Christine Salahub, Lindsay Hedden, Tara Kiran, M. Ruth Lavergne, Sheryl Spithoff, Lauren Lapointe-Shaw
description: areholder-owned virtual health care corporations to provide direct-to-consumer clinician visits: Newfoundland and Labrador, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, and Prince Edward Island (as of November 2024). These virtual care programs are primarily intended to provide access to individuals who do not have a regular primary care provider; however, some programs are available to all residents.

title: Osteocalcin-dependent and -independent metabolic dysregulation in a mouse model of Osteogenesis imperfecta
creator: Josephine T. Tauer, Frank Rauch, Mathieu Ferron, Svetlana V. Komarova
description: Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) is a rare bone fragility disorder. Previously, in a severe OI mouse model (Col1a1Jrt/+), a sex- and age-dependent metabolic phenotype was observed, correlating with elevated levels of the bone-derived hormone osteocalcin (OCN). This hormone is known to play a crucial role in managing energy metabolism, including glucose regulation and fat mass.

title: OmixLitMiner 2: Guided Literature Mining for Automated Categorization of Marker Candidates in Omics Studies
creator: Antonia Gocke, Bente Siebels, Jelena Navolić, Carla Reinbold, Julia E Neumann, Stefan Kurtz, Hartmut Schlüter
description: Omics analyses are crucial for understanding molecular mechanisms in biological research. The vast quantity of detected biomolecules presents a significant challenge in identifying potential biomarkers. Traditional methods rely on labor‐intensive literature mining to extract meaningful insights from long lists of regulated candidates of biomolecules.

title: Synergy Effects in a Bimetallic Ru ─ Pt Alloy Catalyst for Low‐H2‐Pressure Hydrogenolysis of Low‐Density Polyethylene
creator: Yukari Yamazaki, Xiongjie Jin, Weihan Sun, Satoshi Yamamoto, Katsutoshi Nomoto, Kohei Takahashi, Hiroki Miura, Tetsuya Shishido, Akira Nakayama, Kyoko Nozaki
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Hydrogenolysis of low‐density polyethylene (LDPE) under low pressure of H2 has been accomplished with a Ru─Pt bimetallic alloy catalyst. Using Ru5Pt1/CeO2 (atomic ratio of Ru to Pt is 5:1) as a catalyst, LDPE was efficiently converted (97.6 ± 2.5% conversion) to gas and liquid hydrocarbons under 5 bar of H2 at 200 °C, whereas Ru/CeO2 and Pt/CeO2 showed much lower conversion (45.7 ± 3.7% and < 1%, respectively), under the same conditions.

title: Customizing Yoga for Global Diversity: A Comparative Study of Eastern and Western Practices for Effective Integration Into Complementary Healthcare
creator: Sanjay Gupta, Sony Kumari, Nick Vyas, Anjum Padyal
description: Introduction: This cross-sectional study aimed to examine differences in yoga practices to enhance the validity and comparability of yoga research findings. It addresses the "black-box" approach to yoga interventions by highlighting various delivery components that can impact the validity of outcomes.

title: Author Correction: A therapeutic regimen using neoantigen-specific TCR-T cells for HLA-A*2402-positive solid tumors
creator: Yuncheng Bei, Ying Huang, Nandie Wu, Yishan Li, Ruihan Xu, Baorui Liu, Rutian Li
description:
